newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Russia seek to boost trade at Warsaw forum.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Russia seek to boost trade at Warsaw forum.

text.p: Polish-Russian trade is picking up after a long slump caused by the fall of communism in 1989 and is sure to develop rapidly in coming years, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Wednesday.
He said trade with Russia made up only six percent of Poland's foreign trade but was growing rapidly. Russia is Poland's third largest trading partner after Germany and Italy.

"In future, exports to Russia are sure to increase faster than the average rate of Polish exports growth," he told almost 350 Polish and Russian businessmen and goverment officials at a the start of a two-day conference on ways to boost bilateral trade.
Polish-Russian trade plunged on the transition from central planning to a market economy. But trade between the two countries jumped by 35 percent last year to $3.2 billion.

Kolodko said Poland was an attractive partner for Russia because it belonged to the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and would eventually join the European Union (EU).
"For Russia, Poland as a member of the EU can be a door to the more developed markets, as well as the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Slovakia" he said.
Poland needed Russia as a partner to broaden its share of markets traditionally dominated by Russia -- Asia, the Baltic States, Belarus and Ukraine, Kolodko added.
The Polish and Russian Chambers of Commerce, which organised the Polish-Russian Economic Forum, want it to become an annual event held alternately in Warsaw and Moscow.
It is attended by Polish and Russian representatives from the construction, transport, food-processing, chemical, machinery, clothing and banking sectors.

"We want to discuss ways of solving transport problems between Poland and Russia, such as border crossings, which are needed for better trade," Russian Transport Minister Nikolai Tsakh told the conference.
"We would also like to talk about utilising the large potential of Polish shipyards and ship repair-yards in the building of the Russian fleet," he said.

Kolodko said that apart from boosting trade, which the government would support through increased export credit guarantees, Poland would create better conditions for Polish direct investment in Russia and Russian investment in Poland.
